prov.heading: Provision for Credit Losses
prov.text:
The provision for credit losses reflects the amount required to maintain the ACL at an appropriate level based upon management’s evaluation of collectively and individually evaluated loss reserves. The provision for credit losses represents a charge to earnings necessary to establish an allowance for credit losses that, in management’s evaluation, is appropriate to provide coverage for current expected credit losses in the loan and lease portfolio. The ACL is increased by the provision for credit losses and is decreased by charge-offs, net of recoveries on prior charge-offs.

The provision for credit losses was $6.7 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $5.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of $1.5 million and is comprised of a provision for credit losses - loans and leases and a provision for credit losses - unfunded commitments. Provision for credit losses - loans and leases was $7.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, and $5.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of $1.9 million.

nonint.heading: Non-Interest Expense
nonint.text:
The following table presents the major components of non-interest expense for periods presented (dollars in thousands):

Salaries and employee benefits, the single largest component of our non-interest expense, totaled $39.1 million and $37.5 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, an increase of $1.6 million, or 4.2%. This increase was primarily driven by higher incentive compensation, offset by lower health insurance costs. Salaries and employee benefits, totaled $111.0 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to $111.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, a decrease of $593,000, or 0.5%. The decrease was primarily driven by merger-related expenses incurred during the nine months-ended September 30, 2025, and lower health insurance costs, offset by higher incentive compensation.

Occupancy and equipment expenses, net was $3.9 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $4.5 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, a decrease of $659,000 or 14.6%. Occupancy and equipment expenses, net was $12.4 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $14.1 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, a decrease of $1.7 million or 12.3%.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
Our provision for income taxes for both the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 totaled $12.7 million. Our effective tax rate was 23.3% for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 25.5% for the three months ended September 30, 2025. For the three months ended September 30, 2026, we realized a discrete income tax benefit of $1.3 million related to the purchase of Clean Fuel Production Tax Credits, which reduced our provision for income taxes. There were no tax credits purchased or utilized during 2025. See Note 10 - Income Taxes of our Unaudited Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements as of September 30, 2026, included in this report for additional information.

Our provision for income taxes for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 totaled $38.7 million compared to $30.8 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of $7.9 million or 25.6%. The increase in income tax expense was principally due higher net income before provision for income taxes. Our effective tax rate was 24.4% for both the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025.

We expect our effective tax rate for 2026 to be approximately 25-26%.

net.text: We reported consolidated net income of $41.8 million, or $0.94 per basic and diluted common share, for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to net income of $37.2 million, or $0.82 per basic and per diluted common share, for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of $4.6 million, or 12.3%. The increase in net income was principally attributable to a $3.8 million increase in net interest income, a $1.5 million increase in non-interest income, and a $718,000 reduction in non-interest expense, partially offset by a $1.5 million increase to the provision for credit losses.

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income
Net interest income.text:
Net interest income, representing interest income less interest expense, is a significant contributor to our revenues and earnings. We generate interest income from interest and dividends on interest-earning assets, which include loans, leases and investment securities we own. We incur interest expense from interest paid on interest-bearing liabilities, which include interest-bearing deposits, subordinated debt, Federal Home Loan Bank ("FHLB") advances, junior subordinated debentures and other borrowings. To evaluate net interest income, we measure and monitor (i) yields on our loans and other interest-earning assets, (ii) the costs of deposits and other funding sources, (iii) net interest spread, and (iv) net interest margin. Net interest spread is the difference between rates earned on interest-earning assets and rates paid on interest-bearing liabilities. Net interest margin is calculated as the annualized net interest income divided by average interest-earning assets. Because non-interest-bearing sources of funds, such as non-interest-bearing deposits and stockholders’ equity, also fund interest-earning assets, net interest margin includes the benefit of these non-interest-bearing sources.

We also recognize income from the accretable discounts associated with the purchase of interest-earning assets.

intro.text: Byline Bancorp, Inc., headquartered in Chicago, Illinois, is a bank holding company. We conduct all our business activities through our subsidiary, Byline Bank, a full service commercial bank, and Byline Bank’s subsidiaries. The words "the Company," "we," "Byline," "our" and "us" refer to Byline Bancorp, Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries, unless we indicate otherwise. We offer a broad range of banking products and services to small and medium sized businesses, commercial real estate and financial sponsors and to consumers who generally live or work near our branches. We also offer online account opening to consumer and business customers through our website and provide trust and wealth management services to our customers.

lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Deposits
lines.why: Customers' money a bank holds is its business: operating.

lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).
